1.1 RADAR POWER SYSTEM - INTRODUCTION
1.1.1 Purpose
This publication gives the description, technical data and maintenance
procedures for the PDU-200 power distribution unit installed in the radar
cabinet.
1.1.2 Scope
The publication covers organizational level maintenance. It contains:
• A description of the unit and how it works.
• The technical data for the unit.
• Test, inspection, remove and install procedures for the power supply
modules.
1.1.3 How to use this publication
Read the general warnings and cautions in Radar power system - General
warnings and cautions before you do any task. Each procedure starts with the
conditions, personnel, equipment and safety requirements for the task.
1.2 RADAR POWER SYSTEM - GENERAL WARNINGS AND CAUTIONS
1.2.1 Warnings
! WARNING
DANGEROUS VOLTAGES ARE PRESENT IN THE PDU-200 WHEN
MAINS POWER IS CONNECTED. MAKE SURE THE MAIN CIRCUIT
BREAKER IS OPEN AND TAGGED BEFORE YOU START. IF YOU DO
NOT, YOU CAN BE KILLED OR SERIOUSLY INJURED.
! WARNING
THE POWER SUPPLY MODULES CAN STAY HOT FOR UP TO 15
MINUTES AFTER POWER IS REMOVED. WEAR PROTECTIVE GLOVES
WHEN YOU HANDLE THEM.
Obey the warnings above when you work on the radar power system. Each
procedure in this publication repeats the warnings that apply to it.

1.2.2 Cautions
! CAUTION

! CAUTION

2.1 PDU-200 POWER DISTRIBUTION UNIT - DESCRIPTION OF HOW IT IS MADE
AND HOW IT WORKS
2.1.1 General
The PDU-200 power distribution unit receives three-phase mains power and
supplies regulated power to the radar cabinet. It contains a mains filter, two
hot-swappable power supply modules and an output distribution board. Refer
to Figure 2-1 for the block diagram.
The technical data for the unit is given in PDU-200 power distribution unit -
Technical data.
2.1.2 Function
Mains power enters through the input connector J1 and passes through the
mains filter. The filtered supply feeds both power supply modules in parallel.
Each module can carry the full load, so the unit keeps working if one module
fails.
Figure 2-1: PDU-200 block diagram
The output distribution board divides the 28 V DC output into three protected
circuits. The function of each circuit is given in Table 2-1.
Table 2-1: Output circuits
Circuit Supplies Fuse rating
OUT 1 Transmitter control unit 10 A
OUT 2 Receiver and signal processor 6 A
OUT 3 Cooling fans and cabinet lighting 4 A

2.1.3 Indicators
The front panel has one green POWER indicator and one amber indicator for
each power supply module. An amber indicator that comes on shows that its
module has failed or has been removed.
2.2 PDU-200 POWER DISTRIBUTION UNIT - TECHNICAL DATA
2.2.1 Technical data
The technical data for the PDU-200 is given in Table 2-2.
Table 2-2: PDU-200 technical data
Characteristic Value Remarks
Input voltage 400 V AC, 3 phase, 50 Hz Plus or minus 10 percent
Output voltage 28 V DC Regulated to 1 percent
Maximum output current 20 A Shared by both modules
Mass 14.5 kg With both modules installed
Dimensions (H x W x D) 133 mm x 483 mm x 420 mm 3U rack mount
Operating temperature -20 to +55 degrees C Non-condensing

3.1 PDU-200 POWER DISTRIBUTION UNIT - OPERATIONAL TEST
(a) Close the main circuit breaker.
(b) Make sure the green POWER indicator comes on and both amber indicators stay off.
(c) Measure the voltage at test points TP1 and TP2 with the digital multimeter.
(i) Make sure the voltage is between 27.7 V DC and 28.3 V DC.
(ii) If the voltage is out of limits, replace the power supply module. Refer to Power
supply module - Remove procedure.

3.2 POWER SUPPLY MODULE - REMOVE PROCEDURE
(a) Make sure that the amber indicator for the module you will remove is on, or that the
module is the one identified for replacement.
(b) Loosen the two captive screws on the module front panel.
(c) Pull the module straight out of its slot by its handle.
! NOTE
THE OTHER MODULE CONTINUES TO SUPPLY THE FULL LOAD WHILE ONE
MODULE IS REMOVED.
(d) Put the module in an anti-static bag and attach a tag that gives the fault.
